title: The Humming Revachol: A Dialogue Network Analysis of Narrative Power in Disco Elysium
abstract: arXiv:2611.28812v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This study applies social network analysis to the narrative RPG Disco Elysium to examine how narrative power is distributed among its characters. A directed, weighted character-mention network of 73 NPCs is constructed from the game's complete dialogue script, with characters identified and annotated across five social attributes. Narrative power is operationalised through four dimensions: attention, authority, discursive initiative, and embeddedness. Non-parametric statistical tests examine differences across gender, age, race, class, and ideology. The findings suggest that narrative power is largely independent of social identity categories and is more closely associated with character narrative functions, while structural embeddedness reflects the socio-organisational contexts in which characters are situated. translated_title: 嗡鸣的瑞瓦肖：《极乐迪斯科》中叙事权力的对话网络分析
translated_abstract: 本研究将社会网络分析应用于叙事角色扮演游戏《极乐迪斯科》，以考察叙事权力在其角色之间的分布方式。研究基于游戏完整对话脚本构建了一个包含73名NPC的有向加权角色提及网络，并对角色在五个社会属性维度上进行了识别与标注。叙事权力通过四个维度进行操作化：关注度、权威性、话语主动性和结构嵌入性。研究采用非参数统计检验考察性别、年龄、种族、阶级和意识形态之间的差异。结果表明，叙事权力在很大程度上独立于社会身份类别，而与角色所承担的叙事功能更为相关，同时结构嵌入性则反映了角色所处的社会组织背景。这些发现表明，对话网络分析能够揭示单凭可见性计数无法察觉的表征结构模式。
tldr: 本研究对《极乐迪斯科》中73名NPC的对话提及网络进行社会网络分析，发现游戏中的叙事权力主要由角色的叙事功能决定，而非其性别、种族等社会身份属性。
en_tdlr: This study applies social network analysis to 73 NPCs' dialogue mention network in Disco Elysium, finding that narrative power is driven mainly by characters' narrative functions rather than social identity categories such as gender or race.
